observation: GSE120575 (16,291 cells): 1 cell positive for >=2 of 3 specific granule markers (CEACAM8/MPO/ELANE) vs ~0.14 expected by chance under independence; 0 positive for all 3. GSE72056 (4,645 cells): 25 cells positive for >=2 specific markers, of which 19 carry a confident alternative identity from the original authors' independent annotation (12 T cells, 2 macrophages, 5 malignant) and 4 are non-malignant-and-unassigned; 2 of those 4 share patient/well/sequencing-index (apparent duplicate), leaving 3 distinct candidates drawn from only 2 patients.
interpretation: GSE120575's signal is statistically indistinguishable from ambient/technical noise. GSE72056's 3-4 unassigned non-malignant candidates are genuinely consistent with neutrophil identity and are NOT dismissed as noise. What both datasets share is that the recoverable number is negligible (single digits), insufficient to define or map a cell state by any method.
biological_hypothesis: CD45+ FACS sorting followed by Smart-seq2 plate-picking depletes neutrophils to near-completeness, despite neutrophils being CD45+ and so not excluded by the sort gate itself; loss is attributable to downstream handling (dissociation, plate-picking, cryopreservation in GSE120575) rather than absence from the tumours.
clinical_implication: None directly (data-availability finding, not a biological claim about melanoma); establishes that single-cell neutrophil-state biology (H3) cannot be assessed from these public datasets.
suggested_validation: Not applicable to this finding (concerns data availability, not tissue biology). See 08_experimental_translation for assessment via a non-excluding protocol (fixed-cell chemistry, or flow cytometry which does not depend on transcript recovery).
justification: Consistent direction across 2 independent, independently-processed datasets (different labs, years, normalization pipelines) plus concordance with published characterisation of neutrophil loss in scRNA-seq. NOTE: 2 of the rubric's 4 Strong criteria (patient-level statistics, multiple-testing correction) were written for the differential-expression claims in H1-H5 and do not meaningfully apply to an existence/absence claim; this mismatch is stated explicitly rather than assumed away. Replication used dataset-appropriate methods rather than an identical test, because absolute TPM thresholds were found not to transfer between the two datasets (~100x base-rate difference) - itself a secondary methodological finding recorded in REPRODUCIBILITY.md. A prior version of this entry incorrectly stated zero candidates were non-malignant-and-unassigned; corrected 2026-08-01 following audit, see CHANGELOG.md.

observation: Unbiased discovery screen of 35 secreted chemokine/cytokine/growth-factor genes (GO-sourced panel, 327 candidates, 292 excluded by pre-specified detection filter), GSE120575, 19 pre-treatment patients (10 non-responder/9 responder), patient-level pseudobulk, limma. 4 genes significant at FDR<0.05: LTB (logFC -0.72, FDR 0.00025, higher in responders), CCL3 (+0.75, FDR 0.047), CCL4 (+0.73, FDR 0.047), CXCL13 (+0.86, FDR 0.047), all higher in non-responders except LTB. 9 significant at FDR<0.10.
interpretation: The observed direction of LTB expression (higher in responders) is concordant with previous reports linking lymphotoxin signalling and tertiary lymphoid structures to favourable immunotherapy response; this concordance increases the biological plausibility of the finding but is not independent validation, which remains H5's objective using external cohorts. CXCL13 runs opposite to LTB despite canonical association with the same TLS/B-cell-follicular axis in the literature -- flagged as an unresolved tension, not smoothed over; may reflect a different cellular source, addressable by H2/H4, not by bulk pseudobulk alone.
biological_hypothesis: A tumour-derived (CD45+ immune-compartment, see 01_compartment_audit.R) recruitment/lymphoid-organisation signalling programme differs between ICB responders and non-responders in melanoma, detectable pre-treatment.
clinical_implication: None stated yet -- premature ahead of H2 (cellular source), H4 (communication network) and H5 (independent-cohort validation), which this finding is carried into.
suggested_validation: Deferred to 08_experimental_translation until the full body of evidence (H2/H4/H5) is available to evaluate together.
justification: Patient-level statistics and BH multiple-testing correction satisfied; top finding concordant with an independent published mechanism (TLS/LTB). Capped at Moderate, not Strong, because H1 has no cross-dataset replication of its own -- GSE72056 was scoped to H0 replication only (see CHANGELOG.md); external validation is explicitly H5's role via the Hugo/Riaz bulk cohorts, not a gap in this module. Real, stated limitations: therapy-type confound not adjustable at n=19 (anti-PD1 monotherapy skews non-responder 8/12, anti-CTLA4+PD1 combo skews responder 4/5); substantial panel attrition (89% of the 327-gene panel excluded by a pre-specified, not post-hoc, detection filter) reflecting genuine Smart-seq2 sensitivity limits in a T-cell-dominated (69%) whole-sample pseudobulk.

observation: Primary test: 34 of 35 H1-tested genes show significant compartment restriction (Kruskal-Wallis, patient-level pseudobulk across T_cell/B_cell/Myeloid/NK, FDR<0.05); the one exception, RABEP1, is an intracellular trafficking protein not a genuine secreted factor. H1's hits decompose into distinguishable sources: LTB->B cell, CXCL13->T cell, CCL3/TYMP/GPI->Myeloid, CCL4/CCL4L2/CD320->NK. Secondary (exploratory) within-compartment response test: 7 of 27 tests significant at FDR<0.05 (T_cell.LTB, T_cell.CCL4, T_cell.CXCL13, T_cell.CCL3, T_cell.FAM3C, B_cell.TYMP, B_cell.FAM3C); notably the compartment carrying the significant response-difference is not always the dominant-expression compartment (CCL4, LTB). One result, B_cell.CCL4L2, is degenerate (zero expression, zero variance in B cells) rather than a genuine null.
interpretation: The recruitment programme is not one undifferentiated signal: a myeloid/NK-derived chemotactic axis (CCL3, TYMP, GPI, CCL4, CCL4L2, CD320, all higher in non-responders) is distinguishable from a lymphocyte-derived organisational axis (LTB from B cells, CXCL13 from T cells, opposite directions by response). Compartment attribution clarifies that both LTB and CXCL13 are lymphocyte-derived (ruling out a simple myeloid-vs-lymphocyte explanation for their directional tension) but does not resolve why they move oppositely. Regulation can be compartment-specific independent of where a gene is most abundant, a genuinely non-obvious secondary finding.
biological_hypothesis: Distinguishable cellular programmes -- innate/chemotactic (myeloid, NK) versus lymphoid-organisational (B cell, T cell) -- differentially associate with ICB resistance versus response in melanoma.
clinical_implication: Not stated yet -- appropriately deferred to H4 (communication network structure) and H5 (independent-cohort validation).
suggested_validation: Compartment attribution is directly testable by multiplex immunofluorescence or flow cytometry (co-staining ligand with compartment marker); noted for 08_experimental_translation, not acted on here.
evidence_strength: Moderate (primary compartment-attribution finding); Exploratory (secondary within-compartment response finding) -- graded separately, not combined, because they carry genuinely different confidence
justification: PRIMARY: patient-level statistics and BH-FDR correction satisfied; dominant-compartment assignments concordant with established immunology (macrophage CCL3, NK/T CCL4, lymphocyte LTB/CXCL13) -- concordance, not validation, which remains H5's objective. Capped at Moderate not Strong: no cross-dataset replication of its own, same constraint as H1. Near-universal primary-test significance (34/35) is expected given four genuinely distinct lineages were compared, not surprising on its own -- the informative content is which compartment dominates, not that restriction exists. SECONDARY: pre-declared exploratory given reduced power (Myeloid excluded entirely from this test, only 3 usable responder patients; B cell n=11). Real, stated gap: CCL3 and TYMP's response-association (established in H1) could NOT be confirmed as myeloid-driven at adequate power in this dataset -- Myeloid's role remains an open question, not resolved by omission.

observation: decoupleR::run_ulm() TF-activity scores (CollecTRI network, 42,698 edges/1,178 TFs), patient-level pseudobulk, 19 pre-treatment patients (10 non-responder/9 responder), same cohort as H1/H2. 754 TFs scored; 56 significant at FDR<0.05 (148 at FDR<0.10), limma, BH-FDR. 48/56 higher in non-responders, 8/56 higher in responders. Module-clustering characterization (hierarchical clustering + Nyholt 2004 effective-test count) on the 56 hits: Meff=31.3 effective independent programs, 13 correlated modules at r>0.7 (6 multi-member modules, 7 singletons). Two large non-responder-elevated modules dominate: a 21-TF metabolic/nuclear-receptor cluster (SREBF1, SREBF2, PPARA, NR1H4, NFE2L2, VDR, CEBPA-family) and a 13-TF canonical E2F cell-cycle/proliferation cluster (E2F1-5 plus 8 others). A smaller responder-elevated module (IKZF3, SATB2, BACH2) is directionally opposite.
interpretation: The recruitment programme is regulatorily coherent -- driven by a small number of correlated transcriptional programmes, not undirected noise. Reporting 56 significant TFs at face value would overstate the finding; the module-clustering characterization (Meff~31, 13 modules) is the honest summary. The E2F/proliferation and metabolic/nuclear-receptor modules elevated in non-responders, opposed by a lymphocyte-differentiation module (IKZF3/BACH2/SATB2, both established regulators of T-cell exhaustion restraint) elevated in responders, is a biologically plausible and literature-connectable pattern -- stated as plausibility, not independent validation, matching the standard already applied to H1's LTB/TLS concordance.
biological_hypothesis: A coordinated shift toward proliferative and metabolic transcriptional regulation in non-responder tumours, opposed by lymphocyte-differentiation regulatory activity in responders, underlies the recruitment/signalling programme identified in H1 and localised in H2.
clinical_implication: None stated yet -- premature ahead of H4's communication-network component (not yet run) and H5's independent-cohort validation, which this finding is carried into.
suggested_validation: Deferred to 08_experimental_translation until the full body of evidence (H4 communication component, H5) is available. TF-activity inference is indirect; direct validation (e.g. ChIP/ATAC-based occupancy, or E2F/SREBF perturbation in a relevant model) would strengthen this specifically.
justification: Patient-level statistics and BH-FDR correction satisfied; module-clustering characterization prevents overstating 56 hits as independent (Meff=31.3 via Nyholt 2004, non-arbitrary). Capped at Moderate not Strong: no cross-dataset replication of its own (same constraint as H1/H2); TF activity is inferred from expression, not directly measured. Same therapy-type confound H1 documented (same 19-patient cohort) reproduces exactly here, not adjustable at this sample size, restated rather than assumed already covered. This entry covers H4's TF-activity component only -- the ligand-receptor communication component (testing convergence on T-cell suppression) has not yet been run.

observation: Pre-registered exploratory follow-up (CHANGELOG.md), restricted to the primary's 56 locked FDR<0.05 TFs, no new discovery search. Compartment-level (T_cell/NK/B_cell; Myeloid excluded, 3 usable responder patients) whole-transcriptome pseudobulk, decoupleR::run_ulm(), limma, global BH-FDR across 168 tests (3 compartments x 56 TFs). 51/168 significant at FDR<0.05: 43/56 in T_cell (76.8% hit rate), 5/56 in NK (8.9%), 3/56 in B_cell (5.4%). T_cell's result correlates strongly with the primary whole-sample logFC (r=0.887, vs NK r=0.76, B_cell r=0.634) and uses the same patient count as the primary analysis (19/19) -- explained by T cells being 69% of whole-sample composition (03_recruitment/README.md), not treated as an independent finding. NK hits (ZNF395, SREBF1, IRF3, TLX2, IRF2, all higher in non-responder) belong to the primary's non-responder-elevated Module 1/6. B_cell hits (ZFX, IKZF3, IKZF2, all higher in responder) include IKZF3 from the primary's responder-elevated Module 5 (lymphocyte-differentiation cluster).
interpretation: T_cell's high hit rate is expected largely by construction (compositional dominance plus matched sample size to the primary analysis), not evidence of T-cell-specific regulation -- excluded from substantive interpretation. The NK and B_cell hits, despite lower power and weaker correlation with the primary signal, are the informative component: B-cell-localized regulation of lymphocyte-differentiation TFs (IKZF3/IKZF2/ZFX) associated with response echoes H2's own B-cell/LTB finding, extended from raw expression to inferred regulatory activity; NK-localized regulation adds a distinct compartment layer to the broader non-responder-elevated metabolic/IRF programme.
biological_hypothesis: A B-cell-localized lymphocyte-differentiation regulatory programme may accompany ICB response, alongside an NK-localized component of the non-responder-elevated metabolic/IRF programme, layered underneath the dominant whole-sample (largely T-cell-driven) signal characterized in the primary H4 result.
clinical_implication: None stated -- explicitly deferred per the pre-registration; this exploratory result does not alter H4's primary conclusion or any other module's conclusions.
suggested_validation: Deferred to 08_experimental_translation. Not independently validated; may be revisited in H5 or 09_synthesis only if independently corroborated, not acted on from this result alone.
justification: Pre-declared exploratory given reduced power in the informative compartments (NK 16, B_cell 11 usable patients) and given the T_cell component's near-redundancy with the primary result (quantified: r=0.887 correlation with primary logFC, matched n=19 patient count) rather than treated as independent evidence. Same therapy-type confound and same 19-patient cohort as the primary result, not adjustable at this size. Per explicit project-owner instruction, this result is not promoted into Figure 4 or any other main-narrative figure and does not alter H4's primary Moderate-grade conclusion.

observation: Pre-specified Fisher's exact test (target==T_cell x receptor-in-GO-suppression-panel), all scored LIANA-aggregated edges, two response-split networks (Responder: 2,823 edges; Non-responder: 3,477 edges), 4-method consensus (natmi/connectome/logfc/sca via liana_aggregate(), cellphonedb excluded on measured runtime/memory grounds). Result: NOT significant in either network (Responder OR=1.11, P=0.40; Non-responder OR=1.14, P=0.25) -- a negative finding. Descriptive observation, NOT independently tested: among the significant-edge subset (aggregate_rank<0.05), the Non-responder network shows 21/76 (27.6%) T-cell-directed edges with a GO-annotated suppressive receptor vs the Responder network's 6/40 (15.0%), including established checkpoint pairs (CD86-CTLA4, multiple HLA-D*-LAG3, LGALS9-HAVCR2) that emerged from the unbiased GO panel, not a hand-picked list.
interpretation: T-cell-directed intercellular communication is not, in this data, at this sample size, statistically enriched for suppressive receptors relative to communication directed elsewhere -- a genuine negative result, not a failure to look. The checkpoint-pair pattern noticed afterward in the significant-edge subset is biologically plausible and methodologically reassuring (unbiased panel, not hand-picked), but running a new test on that subset after seeing it would violate this project's discovery discipline (the same reasoning that keeps CXCL8/CXCR1/2 out of discovery) -- so it is reported only as a descriptive, hypothesis-generating observation, explicitly not evidence.
biological_hypothesis: No confirmed biological hypothesis from this component -- the pre-specified test found no enrichment. The checkpoint-pair pattern (Non-responder network) is a hypothesis for later synthesis only: if independently corroborated, it would suggest MHC-II/LAG3 and CTLA4/CD86-mediated T-cell suppression is more prominent in non-responder tumours, but this is explicitly not claimed as a finding here.
clinical_implication: None stated -- a negative primary finding does not support a translational implication; the descriptive observation is not elevated to this level either.
suggested_validation: Deferred to 08_experimental_translation and H5/09_synthesis. If the checkpoint-pair pattern is independently corroborated (e.g. against H5's external cohorts), a validating experiment (e.g. multiplex imaging of LAG3/CTLA4 on T cells co-localized with MHC-II+/CD86+ myeloid cells) could be proposed at that point, not now.
justification: The pre-specified Fisher's test is the formal result and is negative in both networks -- graded Exploratory rather than a stronger negative grade (contrast H0's Strong negative finding) because the underlying design is inherently a single-network descriptive comparison (no patient-level replicate at the network level, unlike H0's two-independent-dataset replication), cellphonedb was excluded from the consensus on practical grounds, and patient-pooling within each network is unaddressed. The checkpoint-pair descriptive observation does NOT contribute to this grade and is not itself graded -- it is explicitly labeled Descriptive observation / Hypothesis for later synthesis, not evidence, per the project owner's instruction. Same therapy-type confound and 19-patient cohort as every other H1/H2/H4 analysis, not adjustable at this size.

observation: Pre-registered confirmatory replication of H1's 4 FDR<0.05 hits (LTB, CCL3, CCL4, CXCL13) in two independent bulk cohorts: GSE78220 (Hugo, n=27 pre-treatment, 15R/12NR, limma on log2(FPKM+1)) and GSE91061 (Riaz, n=49 pre-treatment usable, 10R/39NR, edgeR/voom on raw counts -- method chosen per cohort's verified data type). LTB: concordant direction (higher in responder) in both cohorts, not significant in either (GSE78220 P=0.662, GSE91061 P=0.077). CCL3: concordant in GSE78220 (P=0.059) but reverses direction in GSE91061 (P=0.087). CCL4: concordant in GSE78220 (P=0.512) but reverses direction in GSE91061 (P=0.092). CXCL13: reverses direction in both cohorts, reaching nominal significance in GSE91061 (P=0.015) in the wrong direction.
interpretation: Per the pre-registered rubric (direction AND significance jointly required, neither alone sufficient): LTB is Exploratory (direction-consistent, underpowered); CCL3, CCL4, and CXCL13 are Negative findings (direction reversal in GSE91061 specifically, the cohort with the smallest Responder group [n=10] and a different therapy composition than the discovery cohort -- both risks pre-declared before this analysis was run, not invoked post hoc to explain this specific pattern). A technical check confirmed this is not a coding artefact: the same code path in GSE91061 produces a correct, expected direction for LTB, so a systematic sign-flip bug would not selectively affect only 3 of 4 genes.
biological_hypothesis: H1's tumour-derived recruitment/lymphoid-organisation programme (LTB, B-cell-derived per H2) shows the most consistent cross-cohort behaviour of its four hits, though not yet reaching significance externally. The myeloid/NK-derived chemotactic axis (CCL3, CCL4) and CXCL13 do not replicate in this pre-registered test -- no biological hypothesis is advanced for these three beyond the stated negative result.
clinical_implication: None stated -- three pre-specified negative findings and one non-significant exploratory result do not support a translational claim.
suggested_validation: Not applicable to a negative/exploratory replication result. Deferred to 08_experimental_translation only if 09_synthesis identifies independent corroborating context.
justification: Graded per-gene, not averaged into one grade, because the four pre-specified genes carry genuinely different outcomes under an identical pre-registered test (same convention as H2's primary/secondary split). LTB capped at Exploratory rather than Moderate/Strong because direction concordance alone, without significance in either cohort, does not meet the pre-registered bar. CCL3/CCL4/CXCL13 graded Negative finding per the standing rule that a replication verdict requires BOTH concordant direction AND significance -- direction reversal in GSE91061 disqualifies all three regardless of GSE78220's partially concordant (non-significant) results. Pre-declared caveats (GSE91061's small Responder group n=10; differing therapy composition across all three cohorts) are stated as context fixed before this analysis was run, not invoked to explain away this specific pattern. H1's own Moderate grade for these genes in the discovery cohort is unchanged by this entry.

observation: Pre-registered confirmatory replication of H4's two named non-responder-elevated TF-activity modules (Module 1, 21-TF metabolic/nuclear-receptor cluster; Module 2, 13-TF E2F proliferation cluster) in the same two independent bulk cohorts as H5a. decoupleR::run_ulm() module-level score only (not a 56-TF re-screen), limma on module scores for both cohorts (TF-activity score is a continuous model-derived quantity regardless of the underlying expression data's type, same convention as H4's own primary analysis). Coverage near-complete: GSE78220 scored 21/21 and 13/13 members; GSE91061 scored 21/21 and 12/13 (TLX2 below minsize=5 regulon coverage in that cohort). Module 1: GSE78220 logFC=+0.169 (P=0.502, concordant with H4's expected non-responder-elevated direction), GSE91061 logFC=-0.269 (P=0.292, reversed). Module 2: GSE78220 logFC=+0.190 (P=0.134, concordant), GSE91061 logFC=-0.092 (P=0.458, reversed).
interpretation: Per the pre-registered rubric (direction AND significance jointly required): both modules are Negative findings -- each reverses direction in GSE91061 specifically, the same cohort where all three of H5a's non-replicating genes (CCL3, CCL4, CXCL13) also reversed. This recurring GSE91061-specific pattern across two independent pre-registered confirmatory tests (gene-level and TF-module-level) is noted as a factual cross-reference, not tested further -- no new statistical test was run to explain it, consistent with the confirmatory-only scope of H5a/H5b.
biological_hypothesis: H4's non-responder-elevated regulatory programme (metabolic/nuclear-receptor and E2F proliferation modules) does not show consistent cross-cohort behaviour at the module-activity level in this pre-registered test. No biological hypothesis is advanced beyond the stated negative result.
clinical_implication: None stated -- two negative findings do not support a translational claim.
suggested_validation: Not applicable to a negative replication result. Deferred to 08_experimental_translation only if 09_synthesis identifies independent corroborating context.
justification: Graded per-module, matching H5a's per-gene convention. Both modules fail the pre-registered direction+significance rule via direction reversal in GSE91061 -- disqualifying regardless of GSE78220's partially concordant (non-significant) results. Same pre-declared caveats as H5a apply (GSE91061's small Responder group n=10; differing therapy composition across cohorts), stated as context fixed before this analysis was run, not invoked to explain this specific pattern. H4's own Moderate grade for its TF-activity primary result is unchanged by this entry.
